title: Stop a user launch agent from starting at login
summary: A launch agent is a background program that macOS starts for your user account. launchctl disable keeps one specific agent, found by its label, from starting at login. launchctl enable turns it back on.

prerequisites: Know the label of the agent (see the first two steps)
Do not disable agents from Apple (labels starting with com.apple.)

steps.explain: Lists the launch agent files that start for your user account. Each file is named like a label followed by .plist. The label is usually the file name without .plist.
steps.expect: A list of file names ending in .plist, for example com.example.myagent.plist. The list can be empty if no agents are installed for your user.

steps.explain: Shows which services are already disabled in your login session. Read-only, nothing is changed. Look for your agent's label in the list.

placeholders.name: USER_ID
placeholders.description: Your numeric user id. The number is printed by the id -u command.

steps.expect: A list of service labels in quotes, each marked as enabled or disabled. Your agent's label is shown there once it has been disabled.

steps.explain: Disables the agent for your login session, so it no longer starts at login. The change stays after a restart. It does not stop an agent that is already running right now.

placeholders.name: USER_ID
placeholders.description: Your numeric user id. The number is printed by the id -u command.

placeholders.name: AGENT_LABEL
placeholders.description: The label of the launch agent, usually its plist file name without .plist. Use the exact spelling.

steps.expect: Usually prints nothing when it works. Check with the next command.

verify.expect: Your agent's label is listed as disabled.

rollback.explain: Turns the agent back on so it starts at login again. Use the same user id and label as in the disable step.

placeholders.name: USER_ID
placeholders.description: Your numeric user id. The number is printed by the id -u command.

placeholders.name: AGENT_LABEL
placeholders.description: The label of the launch agent that was disabled.

rollback.expect: Usually prints nothing when it works. The agent starts at the next login.

warnings: Disabling an agent does not stop it while it is running now. It only stops the agent from starting at the next login.
Some apps need their agent for sync, updates, VPN, backup or printing. Disabling it can break those features.
Check the label carefully. Do not disable com.apple.* agents or agents you do not recognise.
Do not run this command with sudo. Your own agents belong to your user account.
